decks.notes: The main focus of this Ruby Storm deck is to generate mana quickly and efficiently using cards like Pyretic Ritual and Ruby Medallion, then chain together spells to create a massive storm count. This allows the player to cast powerful spells like Grapeshot or Past in Flames multiple times in a single turn, overwhelming their opponent with a flurry of spells. The deck also includes cards like Ral, Monsoon Mage and Wish to provide additional versatility and ways to win the game.

The main focus of this Dimir Control deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan by using a combination of counterspells, removal spells, and hand disruption. By controlling the board and manipulating the opponent's hand, the deck aims to slow down the opponent's strategy and ultimately outvalue them with powerful threats like Murktide Regent and Kaito, Bane of Nightmares. With a mix of efficient removal, card draw, and strong win conditions, this deck seeks to control the game and dictate the pace of play until it can secure a victory.

This Boros Aggro deck focuses on quickly deploying aggressive creatures and utilizing burn spells to deal damage efficiently. It aims to control the board with cards like Goblin Bombardment and Static Prison while also maintaining a strong offensive presence with creatures like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury. The deck also includes some control elements like Thraben Charm and Elegant Parlor to disrupt opponents' strategies. The key strategy is to apply pressure early in the game and maintain a strong board presence to overwhelm the opponent and secure a quick victory.

The deck focuses on aggressive play and disruption using cards like Thoughtseize and Inquisition of Kozilek to control the opponent's hand while utilizing powerful creatures like Dauthi Voidwalker and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse to apply pressure on the board. The deck also incorporates graveyard hate with cards like Relic of Progenitus and Necrodominance to disrupt opponent's strategies while dealing direct damage with cards like Soul Spike and Fell the Profane. The deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with a combination of creature aggression, disruption, and direct damage.

The main focus of this Boros Aggro deck is to quickly overwhelm the opponent with aggressive creatures like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury. The deck is also built around utilizing cards like Goblin Bombardment and Galvanic Discharge for direct damage and removal. Ajani, Nacatl Pariah serves as a powerful planeswalker to further pressure the opponent. The deck also includes utility cards like Ranger-Captain of Eos for card advantage and protection. Overall, the strategy revolves around early aggression and efficient removal to maintain board control and win the game quickly.

This deck focuses on assembling a powerful combo using cards that do not rely on lands. The goal is to control the game with disruptive spells like Disrupting Shoal and Jwari Disruption while setting up for a game-winning play with cards like Thundertrap Trainer and Goblin Charbelcher. Utilizing cards like Hydroelectric Specimen and Tameshi, Reality Architect, the deck seeks to manipulate the opponent's board state and finish the game quickly with a well-timed Whir of Invention or Flare of Denial.

This deck focuses on utilizing a combo strategy without the need for traditional lands. By efficiently disrupting opponents' plays with counterspells like Spell Snare and Disrupting Shoal, while also controlling the field through cards like Suppression Ray and Whir of Invention, it aims to build up resources with cards like Lotus Bloom and Thundertrap Trainer before ultimately using Goblin Charbelcher to deal massive damage to the opponent. The key is to carefully manage resources and timing to set up the win condition without relying on traditional land cards.

The deck focuses on generating explosive mana through rituals and card draw spells. It aims to effectively cast multiple spells in a single turn, culminating in a powerful combo finish using cards like Grapeshot. The key strategy involves chaining together rituals, card draw, and the use of Ral, Monsoon Mage's abilities to generate a large amount of mana and cast multiple spells quickly, overwhelming the opponent. This fast-paced playstyle requires precise sequencing and resource management to execute the combo successfully and win the game.

This UR Control deck focuses on utilizing powerful spells like Counterspell, Snapcaster Mage, and Flame of Anor to control the game and disrupt the opponent's plan. The deck also includes versatile cards like Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student and Jace, the Mind Sculptor for card advantage and manipulation. Blood Moon is included to disrupt non-basic land strategies, while Murktide Regent provides a powerful threat. The deck emphasizes control through countermagic and removal, with the ability to shift gears and close out games with efficient creatures and burn spells.

The main focus of this UW Control deck is to counter and control the opponent's spells and board state, while also utilizing card advantage and card selection with planeswalkers like Teferi and Jace. The deck includes a variety of counterspells, removal spells, board wipes, and card draw to maintain control of the game. The mana base is designed to support the deck's color requirements and includes utility lands like Field of Ruin and Celestial Colonnade. The deck aims to outlast and outvalue the opponent until it can establish a dominant position and close out the game.

This deck focuses on aggressive plays using a combination of powerful creatures like Territorial Kavu, Ragavan, and Scion of Draco, along with burn spells like Lightning Bolt and Tribal Flames to quickly deal damage to the opponent. The deck also utilizes Leyline of the Guildpact and Leyline Binding to control the board and protect its creatures. Additionally, it includes a diverse mana base to ensure consistent casting of spells. The deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with early pressure and efficient removal spells to secure a fast victory.

The deck aims to ramp up mana quickly and consistently to cast Primeval Titan and search for powerful lands like Valakut, the Molten Pinnacle and Urza's Saga. Amulet of Vigor allows for explosive plays with lands entering untapped, while cards like Scapeshift and Summoner's Pact provide additional win conditions. The deck utilizes combo elements to quickly assemble a game-winning board state with lands that can deal massive amounts of damage to the opponent. With careful resource management and efficient land sequencing, the deck can overwhelm opponents and secure victories in a short amount of time.

The deck focuses on quick and aggressive creature-based gameplay, utilizing cards like Ajani, Guide of Souls, and Ragavan to put early pressure on the opponent. It also includes removal spells like Galvanic Discharge and Goblin Bombardment to clear the way for attacks. The deck aims to control the board with cards like Static Prison and Seasoned Pyromancer while maintaining a steady stream of threats to overwhelm the opponent. The sideboard may include additional removal or disruption cards to adapt to different matchups. Overall, the strategy revolves around maintaining a strong board presence and finishing the opponent quickly.

The main concept of this deck is to control the game through ramping up Eldrazi creatures and artifacts, using cards like Karn, the Great Creator and Chalice of the Void to disrupt opponents while deploying powerful threats like Emrakul, the Promised End and Glaring Fleshraker. The deck focuses on establishing board presence and overwhelming opponents with large Eldrazi creatures, backed up by powerful artifacts like Mox Opal and Mind Stone to accelerate mana production. Overall, the strategy is to maintain control of the game and dominate with Eldrazi creatures and artifacts.

The deck primarily focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy and controlling the game through a combination of counter spells, removal, hand disruption, card draw, and threats that can win the game on their own. It aims to outvalue the opponent by efficiently answering threats while maintaining card advantage and board presence. The deck also includes a mix of proactive and reactive elements to adapt to different matchups and game states.

The key idea of this deck is to cycle through your cards with cards like Street Wraith and Shardless Agent to fill your graveyard with creatures. Once you have enough creatures in your graveyard, you can cast Living End to bring all those creatures back onto the battlefield, while your opponent likely has no creatures in play. This allows you to overwhelm your opponent with a sudden surge of creatures and potentially win the game in one big swing, taking advantage of the synergy between cycling cards and the Living End spell.
